answers.statement: Three problems appear, each in one synthetic source: when persistent parameters make history valuable (Bayes-adaptive), when robust formulations reduce to per-step games, and when per-step randomness can be marginalised.
The sources state propositions rather than benchmarks; metrics are optimal values under a fixed policy class, which matches an equivalence question.
No source contradicts another; each problem rests on a single (synthetic) source, so none counts as consensus.
The idea maps to the first and third problems (persistent vs i.i.d. parameters); the second matters only for interpretation I2.

field_problems.problem: When does persistent parameter uncertainty make history valuable?
metrics: optimal value under a fixed policy class

field_problems.problem: When do robust (worst-case) formulations reduce to per-step games?
When can per-step randomness be marginalised into an ordinary MDP?
